messages.subject: Package reprex
parts:
A tidyverse package, reprex, is designed to make it easier o generate reroducible examples--self-contained code that anyone can run. This seems fairly new. Does anyone from the lavaan community have experience with it? If it works well, it might make life easier for people having problems with lavaan and related.

https://www.tidyverse.org/help/#reprex-pkg

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Package reprex
parts:
Hi Ed

I've never tried to use reprex (despite being someone who does hang around in the tidyverse). 

Another solution is to use a Kaggle kernel. You can upload (or type) code and data to Kaggle, and then you can make it public so anyone can run it, and fork it and edit it.

I couldn't find a public Kaggle kernel that had data that were available, so I created a Kaggle kernel of the lavaan political democracy example: https://www.kaggle.com/jeremymiles/lavaan-test/ .  

I worry that it's too much to ask beginners to do - when they often don't put enough information in an email to answer a question, but it might be worth a try.

Jeremy

Disclaimer: Kaggle is owned by my employer, but I don't have anything to do with Kaggle at work. There are other services that offer similar features to Kaggle kernels, e.g. Jupyter notebooks and github.
